title: I built ORKHOARDE with Tesana AI. Here’s 7 minutes of actual gameplay, and I’m looking for testers
author: New-Specialist6445
selftext:
Hey everyone! I shared a short trailer for ORKHOARDE earlier. Sorry the first video didn’t give a clear picture of what it’s like to play. This one is about seven minutes of in-game footage starting at the title screen. It shows the menus, some of the features in the demo, and what a run looks like from the beginning. I hope it gives you a better feel for the game.

ORKHOARDE is my first game. It’s a free-to-play action tower defense game you can play solo or with up to four players online. You defend four castle gates against waves of orks while trying to keep thieves away from the gold in your keep. The horde gets more organized as the waves and difficulty ramp up. I also built a system that rolls names for champions and bosses, with over 512,000 possible combinations. I’ve submitted the game for Steam Early Access through Tesana. For now, the playable build is on Tesana. You can jump in as a guest or create an account to carry your progress across devices. I also have six DLC packs planned over the next year, each with a new hero, map, and boss.

I spent about 25 days building the first version. I used ChatGPT to make art references and Tesana to build the game and most of the in-game visuals. My workflow was to describe a feature, play the new build, and give Tesana more specific feedback based on what I saw. For example, when a crossbowman clipped through a staircase, I used a screenshot to point out exactly where it was happening. The music and sound effects are separately licensed.

I also used ChatGPT to help set up the Railway backend for accounts and cross-device saves. One bug I hit was that the same account showed about 49,000 XP on PC and 100,000 on mobile. After working through the sync issue, I checked the same account on both devices again to confirm that the totals matched.

I’m still looking for playtesters. If you give it a run, I’d love to know **which class you picked, whether you could tell which gate was under attack, and what made you want to keep playing or stop.** Solo and co-op feedback are both welcome. I’m also happy to answer questions about what it was like building and debugging my first game with Tesana.

Thanks to anyone who watches or gives it a shot!

[Play ORKHOARDE free on Tesana](https://tesana.com/game/orkhoarde)
